scenes.tts: People with severe loss in both balance organs can see the world bounce as they walk. How does a healthy balance nerve prevent that?
scenes.visual: Title card: Report It Twice. A walking figure; the view behind it bounces as it walks. Question on screen: how does a healthy balance nerve prevent this?
scenes.narration: People with severe loss in both balance organs can see the world bounce as they walk. How does a healthy balance nerve prevent that?

scenes.tts: Canals sense rotation; otoliths sense linear acceleration and tilt. Each organ sends both regular and irregular fibres.
scenes.visual: Two organ icons, a canal and an otolith organ, each sending one regular and one irregular fibre. Caption: every organ sends both kinds.
scenes.narration: Canals sense rotation; otoliths sense linear acceleration and tilt. Each organ sends both regular and irregular fibres.

scenes.tts: From here on, we follow canal fibres and head rotation.
scenes.visual: The otolith icon dims; the canal icon and its two fibres stay lit. Label: canal fibres, rotation.
scenes.narration: From here on, we follow canal fibres and head rotation.

scenes.tts: With the head still, both fire fast. A regular fibre ticks like a clock. An irregular one fires with uneven gaps.
scenes.visual: Two spike trains at rest, head-still label: top evenly spaced ticks, bottom uneven ticks at a similar density. Label: made-up spike trains.
scenes.narration: With the head still, both fire fast. A regular fibre ticks like a clock. An irregular one fires with uneven gaps.

scenes.tts: Now a slow head turn. The regular fibre's rate rises and falls with head velocity, how fast the head is moving.
scenes.visual: A smooth head-velocity sine trace; the regular fibre's rate curve rides on it closely.
scenes.narration: Now a slow head turn. The regular fibre's rate rises and falls with head velocity, how fast the head is moving.

scenes.tts: Now a sudden change. The irregular fibre, with its higher gain, responds more strongly, and its spikes lock to the event.
scenes.visual: A sharp jerk in the motion trace; the irregular train shows a large, tightly timed burst.
scenes.narration: Now a sudden change. The irregular fibre, with its higher gain, responds more strongly, and its spikes lock to the event.

scenes.tts: Yet regular fibres detect small motions well. How can the lower-gain fibre win?
scenes.visual: Caption: lower gain, better detection?
scenes.narration: Yet regular fibres detect small motions well. How can the lower-gain fibre win?

scenes.tts: Pause and predict. One made-up fibre has three times the gain, but ten times the CV. Which detects a small, slow turn first?
scenes.visual: Two fibre cards. Regular: gain 0.5, CV 0.05. Irregular: gain 1.5, CV 0.5. Both at rest near 100 spikes per second. Question: which detects a small turn first?
scenes.narration: Pause and predict. One made-up fibre has three times the gain, but ten times the CV. Which detects a small, slow turn first?

scenes.visual: the question stays on screen

scenes.tts: A change in rate counts only if it stands out from the noise. For our made-up counting decoder, threshold is noise divided by gain.
scenes.visual: Equation builds on screen: threshold = rate noise / gain, for a one standard deviation shift. Label: made-up spike-counting decoder. Exact rate noise over 1 s, gamma-process toy, window at a random moment: about 0.65 versus 5.0 spikes per second.
scenes.narration: A change in rate counts only if it stands out from the noise. For our made-up counting decoder, threshold is noise divided by gain.

scenes.tts: The quiet, low-gain fibre wins. Its threshold comes out lower.
scenes.visual: Exact thresholds over 1 s: regular about 1.3 degrees per second; irregular about 3.3. Regular highlighted. Label: made-up model fibres.
scenes.narration: The quiet, low-gain fibre wins. Its threshold comes out lower.

scenes.tts: If our counting decoder must report within a tenth of a second, both thresholds rise, and the regular fibre's lead shrinks.
scenes.visual: The window shrinks from 1 s to 0.1 s; exact model thresholds climb to about 7.1 and 10.9 degrees per second. Label: made-up gamma-process spike trains, not measured thresholds.
scenes.narration: If our counting decoder must report within a tenth of a second, both thresholds rise, and the regular fibre's lead shrinks.

scenes.tts: So what is the irregular fibre good for? Replay the same jittery head motion many times.
scenes.visual: A noisy, natural-looking head-motion waveform replays several times, stacked.
scenes.narration: So what is the irregular fibre good for? Replay the same jittery head motion many times.

scenes.tts: Pause and predict. If irregular spikes were just noise, could their timing tell one motion from another?
scenes.visual: Question on screen: just noise, or timing that tells motions apart?
scenes.narration: Pause and predict. If irregular spikes were just noise, could their timing tell one motion from another?

scenes.visual: the question stays on screen

scenes.tts: Their precisely timed spikes told different motions apart. Irregular at rest, precise when it matters.
scenes.visual: Two different waveforms, each with its irregular spike pattern; the patterns differ clearly. Label: Lacquaniti and colleagues, 2023.
scenes.narration: Their precisely timed spikes told different motions apart. Irregular at rest, precise when it matters.

scenes.tts: Neither channel keeps reporting a steady spin. In a long turn at constant speed, the canal signal fades in both.
scenes.visual: A long constant-speed rotation; both fibres' responses decay back toward their resting rates.
scenes.narration: Neither channel keeps reporting a steady spin. In a long turn at constant speed, the canal signal fades in both.

scenes.tts: So here is the one idea. The nerve reports head motion on two overlapping channels, whoever caused it.
scenes.visual: Callout box builds: The one idea. Two overlapping channels.
scenes.narration: So here is the one idea. The nerve reports head motion on two overlapping channels, whoever caused it.

scenes.tts: In the canals, regular fibres follow how fast the head is turning, in a steady, precise rate.
scenes.visual: Callout line 1, canals: regular, how fast the head turns.
scenes.narration: In the canals, regular fibres follow how fast the head is turning, in a steady, precise rate.

scenes.tts: Irregular fibres add higher gain, more response to how quickly the turn changes, and well-timed spikes.
scenes.visual: Callout line 2, canals: irregular, higher gain, more response to change, precise timing. Small line beneath: otoliths show the same contrast for linear acceleration and tilt.
scenes.narration: Irregular fibres add higher gain, more response to how quickly the turn changes, and well-timed spikes.

scenes.tts: In the head-posture neurons tested, your own turn is largely cancelled, when neck feedback matches the prediction.
scenes.visual: Callout line 3: tested vestibular-only neurons; your own turn largely cancelled; matching neck feedback required. Scope line beneath: regularity is a continuum.
scenes.narration: In the head-posture neurons tested, your own turn is largely cancelled, when neck feedback matches the prediction.

scenes.tts: Fast, precise reports are thought to help hold the world still. Muting matched, self-made turns in the tested neurons may help the head reflex spare the turns you intend.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: report it twice, on two overlapping channels; pass on the surprise, when the neck confirms the prediction.
scenes.narration: Fast, precise reports are thought to help hold the world still. Muting matched, self-made turns in the tested neurons may help the head reflex spare the turns you intend.
